example.question: How does DHL Group calculate free cash flow (FCF) as a management indicator, and which indicator replaces FCF as the management indicator from 2026?
example.question_natural: How does DHL Group calculate free cash flow, and what replaces it as a management indicator from 2026?
example.reference_answer: DHL Group calculates free cash flow (FCF) as free cash flow excluding acquisitions and divestitures (FCF excl. M&A) plus or minus the cash inflow/outflow from acquisitions/divestitures. FCF excl. M&A is itself derived from operating cash flow (OCF): OCF plus or minus the cash inflow/outflow from change in property, plant and equipment and intangible assets, minus the cash outflow for leases, plus or minus net interest paid (excluding leases). FCF is a management indicator derived from OCF that shows how much cash is available for paying out dividends or repaying debt at the end of a reporting period. Starting from 2026, FCF will be replaced as a management indicator by free cash flow excluding acquisitions and divestitures (FCF excl. M&A).

example.question: What was Luzerner Kantonalbank's consolidated (Group) Basel III leverage ratio at 31 December 2025, and how much headroom did it have over the 3% leverage ratio minimum requirement, in percentage points and in Swiss francs of Tier 1 capital?
example.question_natural: What was Luzerner Kantonalbank Group's leverage ratio at end-2025, and its headroom over the 3% minimum, in pp and CHF?
example.reference_answer: At 31 December 2025 the Group leverage ratio was 7.71% (Tier 1 capital of CHF 5,050.6 million over total Basel III leverage ratio exposure of CHF 65,472.3 million, as shown in the Group key metrics; the parent company alone reports 7.61%). example.question: According to Prudential International Assurance plc's (PIA) 2025 Solvency and Financial Condition Report, what was its Minimum Capital Requirement (MCR) at 31 December 2025 and 2024, which element of the MCR calculation determined it (linear formula, cap or floor), and in which tier are the eligible own funds that cover it?
example.question_natural: What was Prudential International Assurance's minimum capital requirement at end-2025, what sets it, and what tier is its own funds?
example.reference_answer: PIA's Minimum Capital Requirement was £35m at 31 December 2025 (2024: £72m); in the S.28.01 template it is £34,684 thousand. The MCR is subject to a floor of 25% of SCR and a cap of 45% of SCR. The linear MCR was only £17m (2024: £16m), below the floor of £35m (25% of the £139m SCR; cap £62m), so the floor is binding: the MCR is currently 25% of SCR, and its reduction is driven by the corresponding change in the SCR. PIA's eligible own funds of £430m (2024: £407m) are all Tier 1 capital (unrestricted): ordinary share capital £65m, reconciliation reserve £277m and other items approved by the supervisory authority as basic own funds £88m; PIA has no ancillary own funds. The ratio of eligible own funds to MCR was 1238.73%.

example.question_natural: What would Belfius Insurance's Solvency II ratio be after a +50bp government bond spread shock, and would it stay above its risk appetite minimum?
example.reference_answer: Under a +50bps credit spread shock on government bonds, Belfius Insurance's Solvency II ratio would fall from the base case of 201% (after dividend, end of December 2025) to 185%, a change of -15pp as stated in the sensitivity table, i.e. 15 percentage points below the base case (the difference of the rounded ratios, 201 - 185, would be 16 points; the table's deltas are computed on unrounded ratios, e.g. the -50bps interest rate shock shows 211% and +11pp). At 185% the ratio would remain above the 160% minimum Solvency II ratio defined in its Risk Appetite framework (and well above the 100% regulatory minimum).
